prompt:
1 of 5. When something breaks, the developers get a problem report listing the problem and the earlier problems that led to it. Priya's team marks a new problem as 'unrelated to the earlier one' on purpose. Should the report still list that earlier problem?
  A) Hide it. The team said it was unrelated, so the report shows only the new problem and its own steps.  B) Show it anyway, in full, so nothing is ever hidden from the developers.  C) Show it, but collapsed and clearly marked 'flagged as unrelated by the team'.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

2 of 5. A problem is marked as 'directly caused by' another specific problem. An unrelated earlier problem also happened just before it. What should the report show?
  A) Always show the named direct cause, labelled as the direct cause, even if other earlier problems exist.  B) Show the direct cause only when no other earlier problem exists.  C) Show both with equal weight and let the developers decide.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

3 of 5. A problem happens while the system is already dealing with another problem. Nobody marked either problem as related or unrelated. Should the report keep showing the earlier problem?
  A) Yes. Show it as now, labelled 'happened while handling the earlier problem'.  B) No. Show only the latest problem to keep the report short.  C) Show it only if the earlier problem was serious.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

5 of 5. The 'unrelated' rule is applied to the problem report on screen. The same problem history also appears in the alert email sent to your admins and in the saved log. Should those change too?
  A) Only the on-screen report changes. Anything that shares the same history logic follows the rule, and nothing else changes, including layout and wording.  B) Change the admin email and the saved log as well, so every place matches.  C) Keep the admin email and the log exactly as they are, even where they share the same logic.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >
typed: A) Only the on-screen report changes. Anything that shares the same history logic follows the rule, and nothing else changes, including layout and wording.
